column3: Repeats faith, righteous deeds, and an unfailing reward almost verbatim.
The immediately preceding command to recite the unalterable Book frames the promise as divine speech.
Explicitly states that God does not let the reward of believers be lost.
Repeats the faith-and-righteous-deeds formula with an unfailing reward.
Within the same surah, believers who do righteous deeds receive a good reward.
Directly joins patience with God's not wasting the reward of those who do good.
God does not waste the reward of reformers who hold fast to the Book and prayer.
The adjacent contrast between devoted worshippers and worldly distraction clarifies the focus's faithful righteous agents.
Within the same surah, faith and righteous action receive the finest recompense.
Defines the world's adornment as a test of who performs the best deeds.
The immediately preceding choice of faith or disbelief supplies the negative alternative to the focus's promise.
Nearby grief over refusal to believe concerns faith, but not righteous action or reward.
Life and death are a test of which people perform the best deeds.

God explicitly promises not to lose any worker's deed and gives the best recompense.

Repeats faith and righteous deeds as the defining marks of the best creatures.
Faithful righteous servants receive glad tidings, and a good deed is increased in goodness.
The surah's closing command joins hope in God with righteous action and unalloyed worship.

The statement of being financially ruined does not clarify faith, righteous action, or divine reward.

Judgment among people in the Fire does not illuminate the focus's faith-and-deed promise.

The youths' faith and increased guidance give a same-surah example of faith being strengthened.
Repeats faith, righteous deeds, and an unfailing reward.
The garden's ruin and regret over association form the immediate negative counterpart to enduring reward.
The unbeliever's presumptuous claim to a good return contrasts with the focus's stated basis of faith and good deeds.
Faithful righteous people receive forgiveness and recompense according to the best of their deeds.

Faith and righteous deeds are explicitly followed by gardens of bliss.
The immediate conclusion calls God the best in reward and final outcome.
Fear of punishment alone does not clarify the focus's preserved reward for good deeds.
God recompenses those who believe and do righteous deeds from His bounty.
Witnessing persecution of believers concerns faith but not righteous action or reward.

Faith and righteous deeds lead to blessedness and a good final return.

God fully pays the wages of those who believe and do righteous deeds.

Faith and righteous deeds are explicitly followed by gardens with rivers and great success.

The trustworthy Spirit's descent does not clarify faith, good deeds, or their reward.
Rejects treating evildoers as equal to those who believe and do righteous deeds.
The prophet's trustworthiness does not directly explain the focus's promise.
Human creation in the best form does not bear on righteous deeds or reward.
The warning to believing people after punishment gives a general faith context without the focus's reward relation.

Honor belonging to God, the Messenger, and believers does not explain righteous deeds or their preservation.

Showy hostile action is encompassed by God, providing a negative contrast to genuinely good deeds.
God's awareness of what people do supplies only a general accountability background.
Following revelation under God's knowledge of deeds is a remote foundation rather than a reward parallel.
The ordinary human lives of earlier messengers do not connect to the focus's promise.
Disbelief bears its own burden, while righteous action prepares a future resting place for its doers.
Faith and righteous deeds are explicitly followed by gardens, the central positive outcome of the focus.
Wholehearted submission and doing good receive a reward with the Lord and freedom from fear or grief.
Unspoiled charitable action has a reward with the Lord, giving a concrete case of preserved good work.

Showy or hurtful charity is rendered barren, a negative contrast to the focus's enduring reward.
Apostasy nullifies deeds, directly contrasting the focus's promise that good work is not lost.
Deeds are nullified in this world and the next for those who reject God's signs.
Those who do good and remain reverent after hardship receive a tremendous reward.

Faith and righteous deeds lead to lasting gardens and a true promise.

Believing men and women who do righteous deeds enter Paradise without the least injustice.
Belief in God and His messengers is followed by the promise of reward and mercy.
Those who believe and hold fast to God receive their rewards in full and further bounty.
Faith, the Last Day, and righteous action are joined to freedom from fear and grief.
God rewards truthful response with gardens, directly linking faithful reception to recompense.
Associating partners would nullify the deeds even of prophets, the stark contrary to preserved reward.
A good deed receives tenfold reward, specifying divine recompense for good action.
Faith and righteous deeds lead to eternal residence in Paradise, with burdens limited to capacity.
Denying God's signs and the Hereafter makes deeds fruitless, opposing the focus's assurance.

True believers receive forgiveness, noble provision, and ranks with their Lord.
Belief, migration, and striving are followed by forgiveness and noble provision.
Believers bound by faith, migration, and striving belong together, extending the faithful-action community.

Those who maintain God's mosques with faith, prayer, almsgiving, and reverence are hoped to be guided.
Faith, migration, and striving establish higher rank and success with God.
God gives faithful strivers glad tidings of mercy, pleasure, and abiding gardens.
God will see people's deeds and inform them of what they did, giving an accountability frame for reward.
God purchases believers' lives and wealth for Paradise, making reward a covenantal divine promise.
God guides those who believe and do righteous deeds, whose outcome is gardens with rivers.
Those who do good receive the best reward and more, closely paralleling excellent work and recompense.
Patient people who do righteous deeds receive forgiveness and a great reward.
Good deeds remove evil deeds, supplying a restorative function for righteous action.
God rewards those who do good, applying the beneficent-worker principle within Joseph's story.
Patient, prayerful, charitable people who repel evil with good receive the good final home.
Those who believe and do righteous deeds enter gardens by their Lord's permission.
Those who do good receive good in this world, and the Hereafter's abode is better.
The good are received by angels into Paradise in return for what they used to do.
Those who emigrate for God after oppression receive a good settlement and a greater Hereafter reward.
Patient people who rely on their Lord clarify the enduring moral stance beside good action.
Abraham receives good in this world and is among the righteous in the Hereafter.
Seeking the fleeting world brings a limited, blameworthy result, contrasting the focus's durable recompense.
Whoever seeks the Hereafter, strives for it as a believer, has an appreciated effort.
Wealth and children are temporary adornment, while enduring righteous deeds are better in reward and hope.
It identifies people whose effort is lost while they mistakenly think they are doing good.
Hell is the recompense for disbelief and mockery, the immediate negative counterpart to 18:30-31.
The faithful righteous recipients remain in Paradise forever, completing the focus's promised outcome.
Repentance, faith, and righteous action lead to Paradise without injustice.
Enduring righteous deeds are better with the Lord in reward and final return.
A believer who comes with righteous deeds receives the highest ranks and abiding gardens.
God is forgiving to one who repents, believes, does righteous deeds, and remains guided.
A believer who does righteous deeds need fear neither injustice nor loss.
A believer's righteous effort is not denied, and it is recorded, closely matching non-loss of good work.
The righteous servants inherit the earth, extending the positive destiny of righteous action.
God admits those who believe and do righteous deeds into gardens with rivers.
Faith and righteous deeds are followed by entry into gardens and honor.
Those who believe and do righteous deeds receive forgiveness and noble provision.
Those who strive for God and are killed or die receive good provision from God.
The believers' success introduces a sustained portrait of faithful conduct and its inheritance.
The faithful are named inheritors, defining the successful outcome of their conduct.
Those inheritors receive al-Firdaws and remain there forever.
Disbelievers' deeds are shown as a mirage and then fully accounted for, a negative work-and-recompense counterpart.
God promises believers who do righteous deeds authority, security, and established worship.
The deeds of rejecters are reduced to scattered dust, opposing the focus's preserved reward.
Patient faithful conduct is rewarded with the lofty chamber and a greeting of peace.
Whoever brings a good deed receives something better and is secure from fear.
Patient believers who repel evil with good receive their reward twice over.
Repentance, faith, and righteous action are presented as the path to success.
Whoever brings a good deed receives something better, while evil is repaid only in kind.
The testing of professed faith supplies the trial context in which good action is made manifest.
Those who strive for God are guided in His ways, connecting effort with divine response.
Those who believe and do righteous deeds are delighted in a garden.
Those who believe and do righteous deeds receive gardens of refuge for what they used to do.
Obedient righteous action receives double reward and noble provision.
The catalog of faithful virtues culminates in forgiveness and a great reward.
Those who believe and do righteous deeds receive forgiveness and noble provision.
Neither wealth nor children bring nearness; faith and righteous action bring multiplied reward and secure chambers.
Righteous deeds rise to God, distinguishing them from vain plotting.
God pays the reward of those who recite His Book, pray, and spend, then increases them from His bounty.
Those who follow the Reminder and fear the Merciful receive forgiveness and a noble reward.
Every soul is repaid only for what it used to do, giving the general justice framework of recompense.
The patient receive their reward without measure.
A believer who does righteous deeds enters Paradise and receives provision without measure.

Believers who do righteous deeds dwell in lush gardens and receive what they desire from their Lord.
God answers believers who do righteous deeds and increases them from His bounty.

Whoever does righteous action does so for themselves, while evil likewise returns to its doer.
God admits those who believe and do righteous deeds into His mercy.
Those who affirm God and remain upright have no fear or grief.
Those steadfast believers are companions of Paradise in recompense for what they used to do.
Rejecting and obstructing God's path causes deeds to be lost, the direct inverse of 18:30.
Faith, righteous action, and belief in revelation bring expiation of evil and restoration.
God admits believers who do righteous deeds into gardens with rivers.
God promises forgiveness and a great reward to those who believe and do righteous deeds.
A person has only what they strive for, providing an action-accountability premise.
Human striving will be seen, linking deeds to disclosed evaluation.
A person will be repaid with the fullest repayment for their striving.
The reward of goodness is goodness, an exceptionally concise recompense parallel.
A good loan to God is multiplied and joined to a noble reward.
Charitable believers receive multiplication and a noble reward.
The offered saving transaction begins a direct faith-and-striving path to forgiveness and Paradise.
Belief and striving with wealth and selves are identified as the better course.

Those who believe in God have their evil deeds removed and enter gardens with rivers.

Reverence for God brings expiation of evil deeds and magnification of reward.
Sincere repentance is linked to removal of evil deeds and entry into gardens.
The faithful moral portrait culminates in people honored in gardens.
The people of Paradise are told that this is their reward and their striving has been appreciated.
The reverent receive success, gardens, and abundant reward.
The righteous are in bliss, the positive final outcome opposed to the loss of rejecters' deeds.
The most reverent giver is protected, depicting a concrete selfless good action.
Giving wealth for purification supplies a concrete form of righteous action.
The devoted giver will be satisfied, completing the recompense sequence.
The reward of faithful righteous people is gardens with their Lord and divine approval.
